clue.text: Cat on brass, possibly, making bull fiddle

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters given are only one possible arrangement of the real word

blocks.note: all ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat sitting on brass instruments might produce something like the noise of a bull fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bull fiddle is an informal American name for the double bass, the largest bowed string instrument.

clue.text: Hospital left nothing right in care of erstwhile anaesthetist

indicators.note: in places the preceding run of short pieces inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: c/o, the postal abbreviation for care of
H is the map and signpost abbreviation for hospital
L for left
O, the figure zero
R for right
erstwhile means previous, former

explanation.surface: An old-time hospital anaesthetist is pictured looking after a patient on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In care of' reads naturally as a phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'care of' is the postal abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A chloroformer is one who administers chloroform, the early anaesthetic, so the word names an anaesthetist.

clue.text: Vagrant died after ulceration from lack of food

indicators.note: after says the death abbreviation goes behind the ulcer word, though printed first

blocks.note: noma is a gangrenous ulceration of the mouth or cheek, found chiefly in malnourished children
d. is the genealogical abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A vagrant's death is blamed on ulcers brought on by starvation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places D behind the ulcer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad wanders without fixed home, which is what a vagrant does.

clue.text: Irishman of old welcoming end of war — and what followed it?

indicators.note: end of asks only for the final letter of the word that follows
welcoming means taking a guest in, so the Irishman holds the letter inside

blocks.note: Teague was an old nickname for an Irishman
the last letter of war

explanation.surface: A veteran Irishman of former times welcomes the end of war and asks what came after.
explanation.walkthrough: TREAGUE is an archaic word for a truce; the R goes in after the T of TEAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is what comes after a war ends, so the archaic word for it answers the question.

clue.text: Strip: riotous conduct with removal of article

indicators.note: removal of says some letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: randan is a spree or riotous behaviour
an, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A striptease show is linked to rowdy behaviour once something is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A rand is a strip, especially of leather on a shoe heel or of land at a border.

clue.text: Hymn from the past begins off-key

indicators.note: a note sung off-key is wrong, so these letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old hymn starts out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To besing is an archaic verb meaning to celebrate in song, which is to hymn something.

clue.text: Store stand becomes 4 inches with this

blocks.note: the opening two letters of stand, the part to be exchanged
as, in the sense of acting in the role of
a hand, used to measure horses, is four inches; H is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A storage stand is said to turn into four inches high with this.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, 'ST as H' turns STAND into HAND, which is 4 inches; the instruction itself spells STASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stash is a hidden store, and as a verb to stash is to store away.

clue.text: Fragrant wood featured in Hans Andersen

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two names

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling wood appears in one of Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanders is another name for sandalwood, the scented timber, especially red sanders.

clue.text: Fatty degeneration set off with one in grip of a drink?

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the word before it is rearranged
in grip of means held inside, so one letter sits within the drink

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
to toss or toss off is to drink quickly, hence the question mark
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fatty degeneration is set off when someone clutches a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that toss, usually a verb for downing a drink quickly, is stretched to mean a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Steatosis is the medical term for abnormal fat accumulating in tissue, as in fatty liver.

clue.text: Prunella, treated in bed, grew haler (12, two words)

indicators.note: treated in suggests being processed or worked over, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: all twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman called Prunella, nursed in bed, grew healthier.

explanation.definitionFit: Prunella is the genus of accentors, including the dunnock, also called the hedge warbler or hedge sparrow.

clue.text: Paddy finds him unpleasant, always lacking in cheer?

ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: An Irishman finds a miserable fellow who never shows any cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy is a nickname for an Irishman, signalling an Irish word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish English a hoor is a cunning or unpleasant fellow, from the word whore.

clue.text: Pâté's spread and then consumed, with nothing in between?

clue.text: Organ's brought up for string band

blocks.note: an organ is a part of the body; the apostrophe s adds S

clue.text: Elegy gents inscribed in kazi

explanation.definitionFit: A lament is a song or poem of grief, which is what an elegy is.

clue.text: Sand eel left off wriggling caught in net

L for left

taken as written

clue.text: Former parliament suffering digs in paper jokily

taken as written

clue.text: Endless assault — had up — when inside gets the gibbet

as in the sense of when

clue.text: Former partners given shelter in safe residence

clue.text: Long-distance runner, not fully fresh as of old
